Extant

/EK-stuhnt/ - the stress falls on EK · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Extant means still existing, not destroyed or lost.

Of the balloon photographs taken over the city in 1906, eleven are extant, and nine of those show the same church.

Worked Example

Wax cylinders warp, crack, and grow mold, and the pianist died obscure; even her own label's vault ledger marks most titles destroyed. Yet four cylinders are extant — two with collectors in Melbourne, one in a university basement, one found wedged inside a player sold at a farm auction. The auction find, astonishingly, still plays.

Extant means still existing, not destroyed or lost, and it is said precisely of things time usually eats. Note what the word does not claim: condition. An extant cylinder may be cracked past playing — extant reports only that the thing itself has not vanished from the world.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

surviving: Surviving is the everyday word for what has come through when much around it was lost, and it fits people as naturally as papers. Extant is the scholar's ledger word for things — editions, specimens, recordings — that time has not yet destroyed, said when counting what remains.

existing: Existing just means in being right now, with no story attached — existing rules, existing buildings. Extant carries the drama of the count: said of things time usually eats, it quietly reports that this particular one has not been destroyed or lost along the way.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

extinct: gone as a kind, forever

vanished: disappeared, whereabouts unknown

Where it sits · how much of it survives — attested → extant → intact

attested vs. extant: Attested is a weaker claim than extant — a lost symphony known only from the printed program of its premiere is attested, nothing more; an extant work, however scorched or stained, still physically exists.

intact vs. extant: Intact goes further than extant: an extant manuscript may be a single scorched leaf, while an intact one has come through whole.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ex-

Prefix — ex-: out, forth

Root — -tant

Root — -tant: standing (Latin stare/stans — the s of stant- merged into the x when English trimmed the spelling)

Put it together

Put it together: Ex- (out, forth) + -tant (standing — Latin stare/stans; the s of stant- merged into the x when English trimmed the spelling) = standing forth. Latin exstare meant to stand out above the surface — what still shows above the flood of time. The picture holds: the extant copies are the ones left standing where everything around them went down.

Use the root in a new word: constant

Use the root in a new word: constant: The cellar's constant coolness keeps the cheese at the same temperature all year.

Root Check

Word Choice

scholarly / technical

Extant is catalog language — editions, specimens, recordings, buildings — and it often follows its noun ("three copies are extant"). Use surviving in ordinary prose; reach for extant when counting what time has spared, and note the contrast baked into its antonym: a species is extinct, but the two museum skins of it are, strangely, still extant.
